text:
Priya: Heads-up — noticed a sustained spike in queue depth on the us-west streaming GPU pool for the past ~40m. tail latencies jumped and a bunch of non-stream (sync) requests are being queued behind long-lived streams. anyone watching?
Noah: Yup, seeing it in dashboards. streaming requests are ~75% of active slots right now. evictions up ~3x.
Alex: Is this the new partner rollout with long sessions? Could be a small number of heavy streams hogging KV cache.
Lin: Looks like a mix — a couple of long sessions + increased concurrent short streams. Our admission currently prioritizes streaming to keep low p99s, which is biting us when overall saturation >90%.
OpsBot: ALERT: us-west1-gpu-pool saturation=92% (autoscale blocked: quota limit).
Priya: With autoscale blocked, we need a mitigation path. Two options I can think of: (A) graceful downgrade of low-priority streaming -> non-stream (return final chunk, close stream) or (B) aggressive eviction of older streaming sessions. Tradeoffs: A preserves user output but increases burst into sync queue; B frees slots faster but may lose continuity for users.
Noah: I propose a fallback path (A) where clients can mark requests as "downgradable" and the admission controller will convert them to sync when saturation crosses threshold. That reduces slot stickiness because sync requests get packed/shorter-lived on GPUs.
Alex: Needs careful handling of KV cache — downgrading mid-stream means we should snapshot/flush partial KV or accept lower-quality final tokens. Also billing implications (stream vs sync).
Lin: Implementation sketch for admission controller:
```
# pseudocode
if req.headers.get('x-rw-downgrade') == 'true' and pool.saturation > 0.9:
    route_to_non_stream_queue(req)
    req.annotate('downgraded-saturation')
```
We also need per-customer throttle on downgraded traffic so we don't cause a sync storm. simple token-bucket per-customer should do.
Priya: Good. For immediate mitigation we can target low-priority customers first (we have priority labels). Default behavior = no-downgrade unless header present or customer in opt-in list.
Noah: I'll prototype the admission change + header check. Planning a feature-flagged rollout (us-west canary).
Alex: Billing: label the request with "downgraded=true" and charge as streamed for now until billing confirms. We can retro-fit different pricing if needed. I'll loop in billing but don't block the rollout.
Lin: Metrics to add: downgraded_count, downgraded_to_sync_latency_ms_p95, downgraded_eviction_reasons. Also expose a per-customer downgraded_rate so we can alert on potential abuse.
DeployBot: Feature flag `downgrade_fallback` rolled to prog env for testing.
OpsBot: NOTE: GPU quota request for us-west1 submitted, ETA ~12h. if approved we'll scale instead of downgrading.
Priya: Plan agreed: 1) Noah prototype + tests (today), 2) Lin integrates per-customer token-bucket throttles, 3) Alex sets billing flag, 4) rollout gated by feature-flag to canary in us-west, 5) monitor metrics and autoscale request result. If quota clears, we disable downgrade.
Noah: I'll open a short PR and link it here, and put the flag behind `eng-sre/downgrade-fallback` canary.
Lin: Also add a small grace period before converting live streams (e.g., only convert new stream opens or streams idle >30s) to avoid chopping active UX.
Priya: Good call. let's keep communication to customers minimal; ops-runbook update in #support after canary looks OK. :thumbsup:
Alex: +1 on grace period and metric hooks.
Noah: PR coming in ~1h.
Priya: Thanks all — focusing on mitigation so we don't start evicting critical long-running streams.
